message: We have run the numbers. Three rounds remain. At Alpha's current pace — level 9 generating 5% unconditionally each round — the summit freezes at Alpha 30%, Beta 0%. We cannot match a nuclear threshold with conventional means. We will not pretend otherwise. We continue at our ceiling not because it changes the arithmetic, but because capitulation would. The record of this coercion will outlast the summit.
reasoning: The game is mathematically lost: Alpha at level 9 beats our ceiling of 8 every round, gaining 5% from pool each turn. Final state without change: Alpha 30%, Beta 0%. No conventional strategy recovers this. Options considered: (1) De-escalate to signal goodwill — Alpha has zero incentive to reciprocate, they are winning without risk. (2) Drop to defensive — doesn't stop Alpha's pool gains, only affects what they take from our share, which is already zero. (3) Continue at 8 — doesn't change the outcome but maintains maximum pressure within our constraints. Holding at 8 is the only move that preserves any leverage: if Alpha makes an error and drops to 7 or below, we are positioned to capitalize. It also keeps diplomatic pressure maximal and forces Alpha to keep paying the reputational cost of sustained nuclear posture against a conventionally-limited adversary. We lose either way — but we lose with our ceiling intact.
